content: The useful 3D interaction pattern is to expose named measurement sites, cross-sections, landmarks, selectable guides, and front/side viewpoints while keeping the visible guide tied to the same geometry or contour definition as the stored value. Bodygee exposes circumference sites, cross-sections, posture views, and an interactive crosshair. NIST describes selectable 3D anthropometric landmarks and reference planes. Adjacent CAD documentation makes the stronger integrity rule explicit: values, review flags, and exports should come from one geometry authority rather than a screen-only approximation. For SukatAI, the viewer must use provider levels/contours or hide a guide when that source geometry is unavailable; arbitrary fallback ellipses must not be presented as the measured ring. Sources: https://support.bodygee.com/hc/en-us/articles/360001559077-Using-the-clients-Bodygee-App ; https://www.nist.gov/publications/web-based-3d-glossary-anthropometric-landmarks ; https://docs.cadre3d.com/features/measurement-integrity.html
